newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields rise to 16.89 pct.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields rise to 16.89 pct.

text.p: Yields on Venezuelan benchmark six-month TEMs rose 80 basis points to 16.89 percent in Wednesday's auction, according to a calculation by Reuters that uses the Central Bank formula.

The Central Bank said it sold 60 billion bolivars of 178- day "monetary stabilization", or TEM, bills with a 16.09 percent coupon for a price of 99.63 pct. At last week's auction the six month notes yielded 16.09 percent

The bank also sold 20 billion bolivars of 267-day notes with a 16.41 percent coupon at a price of 98.76 percent, and 20 billion bolivars of 358-day notes with a 16.74 percent coupon at an average price of 97.73 percent.
Yields for these notes rose 89 basis points to 18.31 percent for the 267-day bills, and 115 basis points to 19.47 percent for the 358-day TEMs.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
